listing_view.reasoning: Demand went from under 1x on day one to 37.5x by close, with the bulk arriving on the final morning — classic retail/HNI chase that usually produces a strong debut. But that same pattern (25x+ against a ₹241–254 band with no confirmed offer size, since the fresh issue exceeds the stated total in the data) means much of the book is flip money, so a strong debut is likely but a weak second week is equally plausible. The unresolved contradiction between fresh issue and total offer size means I cannot even size the float.

longterm_view.reasoning: Revenue compounding at ~33% with EBITDA margins creeping from 10.8% to 11.6% and the latest year's profits actually arriving as cash (OCF-to-EBITDA of 1.36) is genuinely decent operating evidence. Against that: customers now take 111 days to pay versus 86 two years ago, debt has roughly doubled to ₹10.3bn while equity doubled too, and at ~₹254 the ask is roughly 32x trailing basic EPS with no peer comparison, no ROE/ROCE disclosed in what I was given, and no revenue-quality detail in the extracts. The growth is real but it is being bought with working capital, and I cannot tell from this whether the valuation leaves anything for a new shareholder.

governance.reasoning: Clean on the visible surface: no SEBI/exchange actions against promoters [litigation, page 425] and detailed standard conflict-of-interest and related-party confirmations [promoters, page 324]. But the extracts show recurring references to litigation sections and related-party notes without their substance, and the seller's own document affirming it is clean is weak evidence either way — so this is a 'nothing alarming found' score, not a 'good governance' score.

key_risks.why_it_matters: Customers paying in 111 days (up from 86) while borrowings nearly doubled to ₹10.3bn means the growth is being self-financed with leverage; if a large customer slips, interest costs eat the thin 11.5% EBITDA margin.
The fresh issue (₹6750m) exceeds the stated total offer (₹6455m) from NSE's share count, so proceeds use, dilution, and float size are unknown — a material hole before any price judgement.

key_risks.risk: Subscription book concentrated in final-day flows
key_risks.why_it_matters: Subscription jumped from 2.4x to 37.5x on the last day, indicating momentum-driven demand that exits on listing and offers no support to the aftermarket.

key_risks.risk: No earnings-quality or return metrics disclosed
key_risks.why_it_matters: ROE and ROCE are absent from this chapter and no peer valuation exists, so the ~32x implied trailing P/E cannot be benchmarked; buyers are pricing the growth story blind.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A hand-verified offer structure resolving the fresh-issue/total-size contradiction, disclosed ROE/ROCE and a peer P/E comparison, and a receivables ageing breakdown showing whether the 111 days is concentrated in a few power-sector customers. Anchor-investor composition before listing would move the listing view materially.
